articles.title: Auburn stun No 1 Georgia on last-gasp field goal as top-ranked teams fall in successive weeks
articles.summary: Alex McPherson’s 34-yard kick seals 27-24 upset. Georgia lose two interceptions and late fumble. Alex McPherson kicked a game-winning 34-yard field goal as time expired and Auburn, led by quarterback Byrum Brown’s dominant running game, upset No 1 Georgia 27-24 on Saturday.
body: It was the second straight week the top team in the AP Top 25 lost to an unranked opponent after then-No 1 Texas fell to Oklahoma last Saturday. Auburn’s win meant the team ranked No 1 in the AP Top 25 lost in consecutive weeks for the first time since October 1990, according to Sportradar.

Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton led a long game-tying touchdown drive in the fourth quarter but lost a fumble with 58 seconds remaining and the Bulldogs driving for a potential go-ahead field goal.

Stockton, who also threw two interceptions, fumbled on a run from the Auburn 46-yard line. Safety Sylvester Smith-Reed recovered for the Tigers at the Auburn 44. A roughing-the-passer penalty on Georgia’s Gabe Harris Jr helped set up McPherson’s game-winning kick. Auburn players swarmed the field.
“It’s pretty neat,” said Auburn’s first-year coach, Alex Golesh. “I’m really proud of our guys. Really proud of them.

articles.title: ‘Testosterone to burn’: Kagiso Rabada plays down 2018 clash with Australia’s Steve Smith
articles.summary: ‘There’s no hate,’ says bowler ahead of return to St George’s Park. Pair clashed in Gqeberha during heated series six years ago. Kagiso Rabada insists there is no lingering bad blood with Australia as the South Africa speedster prepares to return to the site of his controversial clash with Steve…
body: Rabada has been declared fit to come back from his hamstring tear and face Australia in the second Test at St George’s Park, in his first match since May. The South African’s return comes at a crucial point in the series, with the hosts fighting to stay alive after their 214-run pumping in Durban last week.
But it is also timely, given it was at St George’s Park where Rabada was initially banned for two Tests for colliding with Smith while celebrating taking his wicket in 2018.

Rabada ultimately had his ban downgraded to a fine, leaving Smith and Australia unhappy that the batter was not able to speak at the hearing. The shoulder bump, and ensuing appeal, was one of the final flash points of the ill-spirited series before the ball-tampering scandal overshadowed it all.

Rabada has played against Australia 23 times across all formats since then without issue, while also being a teammate to some in franchise leagues. Speaking to local media before Sunday’s return, the 31-year-old made it clear he had no ill will towards Smith, even if he couldn’t see the pair meeting for coffee.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts placed on injured reserve after Eagles quarterback diagnosed with blood clot
articles.summary: Eagles star sidelined by blood clot in his calf. Hurts sustained injury against Rams on 4 October. Super Bowl MVP must miss at least four games. Quarterback Jalen Hurts was placed on injured reserve on Saturday, two days after the Philadelphia Eagles revealed he had a blood clot in his calf.
body: Hurts was initially ruled out on Thursday for the Eagles’ upcoming game against Carolina. The Eagles said at the time that Hurts had been injured when he took a cleat to his calf during their game against the Los Angeles Rams on 4 October.

Hurts informed the team’s medical staff of the injury after practice on 8 October. The Super Bowl LIX MVP returned to practice the following day before the team departed for London to face Jacksonville.
“Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday (Oct. 10) following the team’s flight to London and walk-through,” the Eagles said in Thursday’s statement.

“The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia.”

Hurts sustained injury against Rams on 4 October.

articles.title: Daniel Dubois delivers devastating second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley to retain WBO title
articles.summary: Dubois underlines status as Britain’s leading heavyweight. Wardley’s corner throw in the towel in second round. Daniel Dubois overwhelmed Fabio Wardley in their WBO world title fight on Saturday night as he continued his quest to become the most authoritative heavyweight fighter on the planet with…
body: After two minutes and 21 seconds of round two, Wardley was rescued from the bludgeoning fists of Dubois by the referee, just as the fluttering white towel of his trainer, Ben Davison, sailed over the ropes in surrender. Davison had been on the brink of throwing in the towel at the very end of the opening round but the bell sounded to end a disastrous first three minutes for Wardley. He was dropped heavily after just 17 seconds as Dubois landed a left cross followed by a pulverising right hand.

It was the first time Wardley had been forced to take a count in 23 fights as a professional and he looked suitably stunned. He seemed helpless as Dubois pummelled him around the ring with a thunderous array of mostly unanswered punches. In the last 15 seconds of the round Wardley was pinned in Dubois’ corner as the punishing blows intensified.
He came out for the second round and, while he threw some wild haymakers and wayward uppercuts, Wardley could not stem the dark tide of punches engulfing him. The end was merciful.

articles.title: Rangers 'pop balloon' as Neil gift wastes chance to go top
articles.summary: Rangers were full of positive energy as they made the trip to Dundee on the back of seven straight wins. However, a Dan Neil error felt "like a balloon popping", says Derek McInnes.
body: As far as optimism goes, Rangers were blown full of positive energy as they made the Saturday-night trip to Dundee on the back of seven straight wins.

However, a Dan Neil error felt "like a balloon popping", said manager Derek McInnes, resulting in the Ibrox side fluffing their chance to move back to the Scottish Premiership summit after a gripping 2-2 draw at Dens Park.
McInnes' men were punished for a disjointed first half when the impressive hosts went ahead through Bradley Fink, but Badredine Bouanani fired in a leveller just before the break.
Rangers lifted their intensity and level of dominance after the interval and were heading for an eighth consecutive victory when Nicolas Raskin slammed in a long-range stunner.

articles.title: Can Hearts prove credentials at scene of title heartbreak?
articles.summary: Hearts' last trip to Parkhead ended with their title dream being crushed in the space of 11 minutes. They return to face Celtic on Sunday refreshed and reshaped.
body: Hearts' last trip to Parkhead ended with their crestfallen players being bundled out of a chaotic Celtic Park and back on to the team bus in their strips and boots after watching their title dream die in the space of 11 crushing minutes.
Meanwhile, the 800 Jambos in attendance - and the thousands back in Gorgie - were going through their own football trauma.
The mere thought of ever returning to the home of the Scottish Premiership champions would have been a harrowing one.

However, refreshed and reshaped, Wouter Vrancken's men are embracing the trip to face a Celtic side still failing to convince a support that are becoming increasingly disgruntled after another chastening European defeat at Benfica.

articles.title: Reedijk has 'sick feeling in stomach' - are his Hibs team in relegation fight?
articles.summary: Two games in, no points gathered and a chorus of boos greeting him at full-time at Easter Road. The honeymoon is well and truly over for Marink Reedijk.
body: Defeat in the new Hibs manager's opening two fixtures means the men from Leith have slumped to the bottom of the Scottish Premiership table.
It's left the Dutchman with what he described as "a strange feeling" in his stomach. So that begs the question: is his gut telling him his new side is now in a fight to avoid the drop?

With Halloween still a fortnight away, it may seem premature to drop the dreaded 'relegation' word into the Hibs conversation. But the fact the green half of Edinburgh is now looking up at the rest of the league a quarter of the way into the season is nonetheless cause for concern.
"I hate it," Reedijk told BBC Scotland after Saturday's 2-1 home defeat by Falkirk when asked about his side's place in the division. "It's something I don't want.

articles.title: After UT loss, Alabama football is in lose-or-stay-home mode | Goodbread
articles.summary: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. − The College Football Playoff won't release its initial standings for a couple more weeks, and won't commence first-round games for another couple months. Matchups will be unveiled on Dec.
body: That's because Tennessee's emphatic 26-10 win over the Crimson Tide put coach Kalen DeBoer's team one loss away from the last place he wants to be: left out of the CFP altogether. Which means for Alabama, every game the rest of the season is, in essence, a playoff game. Any stumble against one of UA's final five opponents − Texas A&M, LSU, Vanderbilt, Chattanooga and Auburn − will vanquish the Crimson Tide to some dying bowl game that might not even exist a year from now.

Last year, Alabama didn't catch its third loss until the SEC Championship Game, but its 10-2 regular-season mark was good enough for a ticket to ride in the CFP. And now, his third UA team sits at 5-2 in mid-October, its margin for error stripped to nothing and its challenge starkly apparent: win them all or win nothing at all.

The Crimson Tide's first-round playoff game? It just drew the Aggies at home. The second round? That's a daunting trip to Baton Rouge. Catch just one loss, and DeBoer will have to brush up on his platitudes again.
"I can't say enough about the hospitality we've been shown by the Duke's Mayonnaise folks."

articles.title: Valkyries retain, relish their Ballhalla advantage in bruising win over Dream
articles.summary: Golden State has yet to lose a playoff game at home; Atlanta had yet to lose in the playoffs. Something had to give, but the Valkyries and an 18,000-strong "sixth man" added up to a defeated Dream.
body: On Saturday afternoon the Golden State Valkyries defended their spectacular home court. They put together another fourth quarter comeback, to take Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, 68-64, handing the Atlanta Dream their first loss of the playoffs and leaving the Dream frustrated.
"I mean, we were right there," said Dream coach Karl Smesko. " Right there. So that's why it hurts a little bit. But it also motivates us."

The Dream were right there, leading most of the game. Until suddenly they weren't. Their lead slipped away in the final minutes, as the Valkyries, led by Gabby Williams, played with composure, the building exploded with noise and the momentum settled decisively onto the Golden State bench.

Williams led all scorers with 26 points, including eight key points down the stretch. This week she revealed to the media how much she likes math and how, in her head, she breaks the game down into possessions and points.

articles.title: Van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Van Veen makes history
articles.summary: Dutch favourite Michael van Gerwen suffered a shock second-round exit at the Dutch Darts Championship on Saturday, losing 6-5 to Irishman William O'Connor.
body: The defeat extends Van Gerwen's poor run of form, having lost his opening match at four European Tour events this season before arriving in Maastricht: the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix, Flanders Darts Trophy and Swiss Darts Trophy. It marks his most first-round exits in a single season since the tour began in 2012.
O'Connor produced a superb display, firing in three ton-plus checkouts of 136, 131 and 121 to seal his victory and book his place in round three.
Elsewhere on Saturday, Gerwyn Price's return to the stage ended in glory as he beat Scott Williams 6-3, while Gian van Veen broke the European Tour record average.
Martin Schindler and Stephen Bunting also jumped into the qualification spots for Dortmund.

articles.title: Rangers miss chance to go top as Jones earns Dundee a point
articles.summary: Callum Jones scored a second-half equaliser as Rangers were held to a 2-2 draw by Dundee and missed the chance to go top of the Scottish Premiership.
body: Dundee opened the scoring when Rangers failed to deal with a routine long ball, with Bradley Fink capitalising to round the goalkeeper and slide home.
The lead did not last long, though, as Badredine Bouanani cut inside and curled in a stunning equaliser to open his account for Rangers.
Nico Raskin scored the goal of the game when his shot from outside the area went in off the underside of the crossbar.
But Jones then caught Dan Neil dwelling on the ball and nicked it off the Rangers captain to slot home the Dundee equaliser.
